A hand-built payload would have been a SECOND implementation of the state derivation, which is the defect class this repository's instruments exist to catch.
assertions: every cell declaring a state carries EXACTLY ONE state mark, so a cell drawn as two of the four (the collapse) FAILS
the fixture exercised all four states across the surfaces, or the test fails

contradicted.detail: web/app.js and web/index.html are unmodified in PR #76. The lenses are served as fully rendered pages from src/server.mjs at /lens/public-works and /lens/fire-ems, with the payloads at /api/lenses/*/dashboard. The reason is that a client painter for these two bodies does not exist yet and a painter that silently renders nothing is worse than a served page; the served page is also the surface both instruments can actually be pointed at. contradicted.what: The implication that 'check.mjs passes' could be satisfied by pointing the existing instruments at built markup.
contradicted.detail: The artboard readers are anchored on inline-style signatures the product's stylesheets never emit, so they match zero on built markup. The bridge therefore had to be a NEW reader, and it is self-tested in both directions against the old one so neither can score the other's form.

contradicted.what: The two-regions requirement read as a layout preference.
contradicted.status: BROADER, and it is the reason the surfaces carry buttons

The only <button> elements on either blocked surface are those tab switchers, which is also what makes the no-retry assertion a counted fact rather than a claim: the buttons that exist are enumerated and none of them re-fetches.

LESSON: An instrument anchored on a RENDERING FORM does not survive a change of renderer. Both of these check.mjs read the artboards' INLINE STYLES, which the product emits as stylesheet classes. Pointed at built markup the old readers matched zero, and zero-matched green is indistinguishable from a pass. The fix is not to make the old reader looser: it is a second reader plus self-tests asserting, in both directions, that neither reader can see the other's form.

An acceptance clause that says 'cannot-occur is distinguishable from measured zero and from unmeasured' is a claim about EXCLUSIVITY, not coverage. A test that counts four states passes on a surface where one cell carries two marks. Assert that each cell carries exactly one, and the collapse becomes a failure instead of a tally.

A 'no retry affordance' requirement is only honest if the buttons that DO exist are enumerated. Counted here: the only buttons on the blocked surfaces are region tab switchers, which the two-regions-of-different-units requirement makes necessary. 'No retry' and 'no buttons at all' are different requirements and conflating them would have meant deleting a required control.

A gate in a dispatch can be owned by the dispatch's OWN lane. This lane could not start G-153's successor until this lane's close existed, and it was this lane that owed it. Filing a close is sometimes a prerequisite rather than an epilogue.
deploy_on_push being unset is the reason 'merged' and 'shipped' are separate words in this program: four routes 404 on two apps even though one of them tracks main, because nothing redeploys main.
DEAD_END: Pointing the existing artboard readers at built markup. They match zero there and would have returned a green verdict on an unread surface.
Writing the four-state fixture as a hand-built payload. It would have been a second implementation of the state derivation, agreeing with the renderer today and free to drift silently.

Building a client-side painter for these two bodies in this lane. The painter needs the payload's derived rendering model to travel with it, and shipping a painter that silently renders nothing would have hidden the surface rather than served it.

Reporting the absence of a violate.mjs in either design folder as a defect. Both embed their violation proof as self-tests in check.mjs, which is the older convention and is explicitly not a defect per A-139.
